text:
jon: Heads up — noticed GH Actions run for infra PRs isn't reliably causing Atlantis to plan/apply before ArgoCD syncs, which sometimes leads to ArgoCD applying an intermediate commit. Repro steps below, anyone seen this?

maya: Seen something similar last week in payment services. Do you have a minimal repro?

jon: Repo: infra/services/payment. Workflow runs `make fmt` and then commits + pushes from the runner. Steps: open PR -> workflow commits a fixup -> git push (from runner). After merge we sometimes see ArgoCD sync the repo before Atlantis apply finished.

devx: FYI our GH app subscription only sends certain events. Atlantis expects PR updates (pull_request.synchronize) but pushing from a job might not trigger the same ordering.

jon: Here's the relevant workflow snippet: ```yaml
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  fmt:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - run: make fmt
      - run: git commit -am "fmt" || echo "no changes"
      - run: git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/${{ github.head_ref }}
```

alice: If the workflow only lists `pull_request` the push inside the job won't create a new `pull_request` event, but GH will emit a `synchronize` for the PR branch. Could be a timing thing where ArgoCD sees the push to the target branch (after merge) before Atlantis finishes apply.

infra-bot: note: received atlantis webhook: "pull_request.synchronize" pr#42 at 2025-06-03T12:05:21Z — plan started, plan finished: success.

maya: I suspect ordering: GH Actions pushes a commit -> webhook to ArgoCD triggers auto-sync on repo change -> Atlantis then processes plan/apply and sets status checks, but too late for ArgoCD on merged main. ArgoCD doesn't know about Atlantis state so it just follows git.

jon: Exactly. We want to ensure Atlantis apply (or at least a commit-status) exists before ArgoCD auto-sync acts on that commit. Options?

alice: Ideas: 1) Stop pushing from CI in infra repos (enforce pre-commit locally or use PR bot). 2) Gate ArgoCD syncs on a commit status / check-run (e.g., require `atlantis/apply` success). 3) Add a short buffer/delay in ArgoCD webhook processing to allow Atlantis to reconcile. 4) Add a tiny controller that filters webhook events and checks GitHub combined status.

devx: (2) seems robust: add a webhook proxy that inspects commit check-runs and only forwards the push to ArgoCD when the required check-run is present and successful. Fast to implement and doesn't require wide workflow changes.

sre-ops: I'm +1 on the webhook proxy. We can implement a Cloud Run / Lambda that receives GitHub push webhooks, calls the Checks API for the head SHA, verifies presence of `redwood/atlantis-apply` or `redwood/atlantis-plan` status, and forwards the event if OK. Fallback: forward after X seconds if check never appears.

jon: Can someone prototype the webhook proxy? If so we can patch the argocd webhook to point to proxy. I'll open a ticket with the repo list.

alice: I'll take the prototype. Will also update infra docs to discourage in-PR pushes from GH Actions for infra repos. Ping me with a short spec. :thumbsup:

maya: quick note — also check atlantis server concurrency/queueing, if apply is queuing behind other applies that could extend delay.

jon: good call. I'll check Atlantis queue depth and add it to the ticket. Thanks everyone.
